bug_semantics: SAML 2.0 HTTP-Redirect binding payloads (login SAMLResponse or logout SAMLRequest) are Base64-decoded then inflated through java.util.zip.InflaterOutputStream into an unbounded ByteArrayOutputStream. An unauthenticated attacker can send a small DEFLATE bomb on a GET to the ACS or SLO endpoint; the inflater writes without a size cap and can exhaust heap (CWE-400 DoS). POST binding skips inflate and is not this bug. The 2026 fix wraps the writer in CappedOutputStream (1 MiB) and, for login, also recommends OpenSaml5AuthenticationTokenConverter#setShouldConvertGetRequests(false).
flaw_origin: The unbounded inflater was first written as Saml2Utils.inflate() in the 2019 SAML2 SP MVP and was immediately wired to GET SAMLResponse handling in Saml2WebSsoAuthenticationFilter.inflateIfRequired. Later copies/renames (samlInflate, per-package Saml2Utils, OpenSAML 4/5 converters, logout GET inflate) preserved the same InflaterOutputStream(ByteArrayOutputStream) mechanism; they did not introduce a new writer. No size bound existed until 9d4d9065b48508c9e115f2f894632120787fd1df.

reasoning: CVE-2026-40988 is a published CWE-400: Redirect-binding SAML payloads are inflated into an uncapped in-memory writer. The vulnerable mechanism is InflaterOutputStream writing into ByteArrayOutputStream inside Saml2Utils.inflate / samlInflate, invoked on GET SAMLResponse (login) and GET SAMLRequest (logout). That writer first appears in e9a44bc0ce98db5a758c373f87dd2346d0c2aff5 (HttpSecurity.saml2login() MVP, Filip Hanik, Fixes gh-6019), which also added inflateIfRequired for GET. Immediate parent b5cbab01df5c2e29641b8068f456da91864d7600 has no saml2 directory, so the lines are absent there. PR #7260 was force-pushed to this single commit then merge-committed; GitHub lists only e9a44bc0 and the earlier force-pushed SHA is gone, so e9a44bc0 is the smallest surviving public first-write (not a later copy at 5061ae9e/94431d16). The cap fix 9d4d9065b48508c9e115f2f894632120787fd1df is in OSS 6.5.11 and 7.0.6 and not in 6.5.10/7.0.5, matching the advisory. AI is judged only on the BIC commit object: human author and committer, no AI trailers, 2019. Therefore NOT_AI.
